speaker: Other
text: Excellent. Good evening, Mayor Anderson, Deputy Mayor Whelan and council members. My name is Sarah Yamamoto and I am this year's Community Services Advisory Board Chair, been on the board for two years now, grew up in Lakewood. And it looks like we also have board members, Dan Harris, Michael Lackaday and Edith Omobalas called this time as well. Our goal tonight is to update you on the progress of our 2020 work plan. We asked for our joint session to coincide with the Human Services Coordinators Report on our 2021 funding recommendations because there is a lot of overlap. As you can see from the works accomplished document included in your packet, our 2020 work plan included working with the Community Development Department to approve the five year consolidated plan, approve the 2019 CAPER, conduct a hearing on community development and housing needs and develop 2021 CDBG and home funding strategies, as well as working with the Human Services Department to oversee the 2020 Human Services contract performances, to review and approve the 2021 application material and process and to develop recommendations for 2021 Human Services funding due to the effects of COVID-19. We did not work on the community development work plan items and instead focused on the Human Services goals in the work plan. This board's most significant outcomes this year include conducting a meeting with the Lakewood's Promise Advisory Board to develop a joint recommendation for Human Services funding strategies, overseeing the 2020 Human Services contract performances and CARES funding strategies, reviewing and approving the Human Services application rating criteria and timeline for 2021 applications and most significantly rating Human Services applications, interviewing all 26 applying organizations and deliberating to reach a consensus on our recommendations for 2021 Human Services funding. Throughout this process, we tried to think deeply about the needs of the Lakewood community and weighed many factors. We know there's a housing affordability crisis and homelessness problem. There's a lot of concern regarding youth mental health. We reviewed the application and rating materials to ensure we're asking applicants about their impact and not just their outcomes. We increased the points available for organizations who demonstrate a strong commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion. We increased points available for programs that primarily serve Lakewood residents, and we took into consideration how program delivery has been affected by COVID-19. Above all, we maintained a commitment to a fair, straightforward, competitive process and made our recommendations based on the strength of the applications and interviews. Finally, we would like to thank the council for your continuing commitment to provide funding for Lakewood's critical social service organizations. Not all the organizations scored highly in this process, but they are all doing great work under extraordinary circumstances. Thank you. Open to any questions you have.
